newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Micron sinks, Applied Materials up.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Micron sinks, Applied Materials up.

text.p: Shares of Micron Technology Inc sunk in pre-opening trading after Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlack cut the stock's rating and profit estimates, according to a market source.
Micron shares were trading at 47, down 3-1/8 from its Tuesday closing price of 50-1/8, traders said.

Kurlack cut the stock to a near-term neutral from near-term accumulate and to a long-term accumulate from a long-term buy, the source said, and cut the fiscal fourth quarter estimate to $0.59 from $0.70. He cited pricing pressure for 64 megabyte chips.

The stock has come down sharply over the past two days as other Wall Street investment houses have said they expect lower profits for the Boise, Idaho chip maker due to falling prices for memory chips. On Tuesday, Micron fell 4-15/16.
On the bullish side, Applied Materials Inc shares shot higher in early trading, moving up 4-1/4 to 94-3/4 after its third quarter earnings came in, easily beating Wall Street analysts' estimates.

Applied Materials, the biggest manufacturer of chip making equipment, said it had profit from operations of $0.77 a share, compared with $0.92 last year. Wall Street had expected Applied Materials to show up with earnings of $0.68 a share.
